predecessors.name: Western Satraps
predecessors.text: the north-western part of the Vakataka shape of 260, which Cliopatria takes from the Western Satraps shape

successors.name: Kalachuris of Mahishmati
successors.text: the northern Vakataka lands (Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, the Gujarat edge) that the Kalachuris of Mahishmati took

successors.name: Vishnukundina dynasty
successors.text: the eastern Vakataka lands in Telangana and Andhra, taken by the Vishnukundinas

successors.name: Kadamba dynasty
successors.text: the southern Vakataka lands (Kuntala) that the Kadambas 'also seem to have' taken (Harishena page); Kadamba page: Ravivarma's suzerainty extended over the former Vakataka lands 'probably sometime…

successors.name: Chalukyas of Badami
successors.text: by about 550 'the Chalukyas of Badami held most former Vakataka territory' (Harishena page)

ledger.x: c. 250: Vindhyashakti founds the Vakataka dynasty in the Deccan. Infobox 'Established: c. 250'; Vindhyashakti 'r. 250-270', his name 'derived from the name of the goddess Vindhyavasini'. The page gives no land for him; the Vidarbha core is the researcher's reading of where the later branches ruled.

c. 260: the Vakataka shape takes the north-western part of the Western Satraps' land. The Vakataka infobox lists the Western Satraps among its predecessors; Cliopatria's Western Satraps shape drops 453 cells in 260 and the Vakataka shape starts at 574,588 km2. The page gives no date; the Narmada frontier is…

c. 260: the rest of the 260 shape. Pravarasena I page: his rule 'covered almost the whole of the Deccan between the Narmada and Krishna rivers', with a sphere 'over Malwa, Gujarat, Andhradesha, and southern Koshala' and four Ashvamedhas; the dynasty page adds 'He annexed the kingdom of Purika which was being ruled by…

c. 260: Bundelkhand, the northern seat of the dynasty, is added to the Cliopatria shape. Vakataka dynasty page: Pravarasena I 'certainly ruled from Bundelkhand in the north'; Pravarasena I page: capital Kanchanaka = Nachna, Panna district. The year is…

c. 336: Bundelkhand leaves the Vakataka shape. Pravarasena I page: at his death (c. 335) 'these provinces seem to have become independent', the Nandivardhana branch passes to Rudrasena I and Sarvasena founds the Vatsagulma branch; the capital moves south (identity). The page does not say who held Bundelkhand…

c. 353: Chhattisgarh and Odisha pass to the Gupta shape. Cliopatria's Vakataka shape drops 924 cells on 353, 345 to the Gupta. Samudragupta page: Mahendra of Kosala and Vyaghraraja of Mahakantara are among the Dakshinapatha kings he defeated; Prithivishena I page: the Vakatakas 'seem to have retained considerable…

c. 353: the south-west (north Karnataka and south Maharashtra) leaves the Vakataka shape for the new Kadamba row. Kadamba page: Mayurasharma founded the kingdom c. 345 and Kangavarma (c. 365) 'had to fight the Vakataka might to protect his kingdom'; Prithivishena I page: Vindhyasena's conquest of Kuntala…

c. 360: Vyaghradeva of Nachna-Ganj acknowledges Prithivishena I. Prithivishena I page (r. c. 360-385): inscriptions found at Nachna and Ganj 'refer to a local king named Vyaghradeva who claims to have been a vassal of the Vakataka king Prithivishena'. The year is the reign's start; Bundelkhand is the researcher's…
385: Prithivishena I's reign ends and with it Vyaghradeva's claimed vassalage.

c. 390: the Vakataka kingdom under Prabhavatigupta's regency is 'practically a part of the Gupta empire'. Prabhavatigupta page (opened 2026-10-19): 'she effectively ruled the Vakataka Empire as regent from about 390 to 410', her husband Rudrasena II died after 'only about five…

c. 410: the regency ends. Prabhavatigupta page: the regency ran 'from about 390 to 410'; Divakarasena 'never ascended' the throne and was succeeded by his younger brother Damodarasena (Pravarasena II) 'around 410'. Mirrors gupta-empire /ledger (vassal_end 410).…

c. 445: Narendrasena drives the Guptas and Nalas from Nandivardhana. 'Around 445 CE, during the final years of Kumaragupta I's reign' he 'reclaimed his former capital by driving out the combined forces of the Guptas and Nalas'. Zone: the Gupta land Cliopatria hands to the Vakataka in 451.

c. 451: the Vakataka shape takes Gupta land in Malwa, Mekala and Kosala. Narendrasena page: 'Narendrasena's authority was acknowledged by the rulers of Kosala, Mekala, and Malava' (an assertion 'many historians' see as exaggeration). Year is Cliopatria's.

c. 451: 180 cells of Cliopatria's 451 shape (Maharashtra 132, Andhra 21, Chhattisgarh 16, Telangana 10) that were not Gupta land. Narendrasena page (r. c. 455-480): the campaign against the Nala king of Bastar 'may have led to the further extension of Vakataka authority, especially in the area around present-day…

c. 461: the contest ends with Skandagupta's recovery of Malwa. 'Malwa wasn't under Vakataka for long as it was recaptured by Skandagupta'; the Skandagupta page's c. 460-461 inscription speaks of a 'tranquil reign'. Year bridged.
c. 461: Malwa returns to the Gupta. The Mekala and Kosala part stays Vakataka. 'Malwa wasn't under Vakataka for long as it was recaptured by Skandagupta'. Year bridged.

c. 480: the seat passes to Vatsagulma (Washim). Vakataka page: after Prithivishena II's death in 480 'his kingdom was probably annexed by Harishena of the Vatsagulma branch', the infobox capital being Vatsagulma.

c. 490: Malwa returns to the Vakataka shape. Harishena page (r. c. 480-510): the minister Varahadeva's Ajanta inscription describes the king's influence over Avanti among other countries; Vakataka page, citing the Cave XVI inscription: he conquered Avanti (Malwa). Cliopatria's Vakataka shape of 490 is the 451 outline…

c. 510: the Vakataka dynasty ends with Harishena. Infobox 'c. 250 to c. 510'; Harishena page: 'seems to have occurred very rapidly after Harishena's death in about 510', 'the Vakataka dynasty came to an end not long after the death of Harishena'; the Vakataka page: 'The end of the dynasty is unknown.' The Kalachuris…

wars.name: Pravarasena I's conquests
wars.outcome: Pravarasena I 'carried his arms to the Narmada in the north', annexed the kingdom of Purika and performed four Ashvamedhas; the page dates no campaign.

wars.name: Narendrasena's war with the Guptas and Nalas
Prithivishena II against the Vishnukundinas
wars.outcome: Prithivishena II 'was defeated by the Vishnukundina king Madhava Varma II'; the page gives no date or land.

wars.name: Harishena's campaigns
wars.outcome: Harishena's minister's Ajanta inscription claims influence over Kuntala, Avanti, Kalinga, Koshala, Lata, Andhra and Trikuta; the drawn Vakataka shape reaches Avanti, Kosala and Andhra only.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a boundary line; the Narmada, the Tungabhadra and the Arabian Sea are the page's approximate limits.
